identification: Planished (hand-hammered all over) silver footed beaker / christening cup, H 8 cm, flared tapering body on a stepped spreading foot with reeded edge, gilt-looking interior wash. Engraved in serif capitals 'BILLIE / 1927' (read clearly at 4x crop; Sonnet's 'BILINE' doubt resolved). Underside of foot: a long narrow rectangular punch reading vertically, about 7-8 characters, consistent with 'STERLING' but not legible letter by letter; opposite it a separate maker's punch: a lozenge (diamond) divided by a cross into four (like the Japanese 'Takeda-bishi' device, or a square/cross device turned 45 degrees). No British hallmark set, no date letter, no town mark. So a non-British piece marked STERLING: American, Australian, or Asian export (Japan/China made hammered beakers marked STERLING with a pictorial maker punch for Western buyers in the 1920s-30s). Maker NOT identified.

viewing_check: WEIGH IT (grams) and read the max off the scale. Loupe the rectangular stamp (STERLING? 925? any town or 'HAND WROUGHT') and the cross-in-lozenge punch (any letters inside it, Japanese/Chinese characters near it). Check foot join, splits at rim, and that the gilt interior is wash not brass showing.
